q: 3 pumps, working 8 hours a day, can empty a tank in 2 days. How many hours a day must 4 pumps work to empty the tank in 1 day?
s: Let the required number of working hours per day be x. More pumps, Less working hours per day (Indirect Proportion) Less days, More working hours per day (Indirect Proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Pumps 4}}:3 \\ {\text{Days}}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{1}}:2 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::8:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 4 \times 1 \times x = 3 \times 2 \times 8 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{ {3 \times 2 \times 8} }}{{ 4 }} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 12 \end{aligned}$$

q: If the cost of x metres of wire is d rupees, then what is the cost of y metres of wire at the same rate?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Cost of }}x{\text{ metres}} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{. }}d \\ & {\text{Coast of 1 metre}} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {\frac{d}{x}} \right) \\ & {\text{Cost of }}y{\text{ metres}} \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}}\left( {\frac{d}{x} \times y} \right) \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.}} {\frac{{yd}}{x}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Running at the same constant rate, 6 identical machines can produce a total of 270 bottles per minute. At this rate, how many bottles could 10 such machines produce in 4 minutes?
s: Let the required number of bottles be x . More machines, More bottles (Direct Proportion) More minutes, More bottles (Direct Proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Machines}}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{6}}:10 \\ {\text{Time(in min}}{\text{.)}}\,\,{\text{1}}:4 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::270:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 6 \times 1 \times x = 10 \times 4 \times 270 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{ {10 \times 4 \times 270} }}{{ 6 }} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 1800 \end{aligned}$$

q: A fort had provision of food for 150 men for 45 days. After 10 days, 25 men left the fort. The number of days for which the remaining food will last, is:
s: After 10 days : 150 men had food for 35 days. Suppose 125 men had food for x days. Now, Less men, More days (Indirect Proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 125:150::35:x \\ & \Rightarrow 125 \times x = 150 \times 35 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{150 \times 35}}{{125}} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 42 \end{aligned}$$

q: 39 persons can repair a road in 12 days, working 5 hours a day. In how many days will 30 persons, working 6 hours a day, complete the work?
s: Let the required number of days bex. Less persons, More days (Indirect Proportion) More working hours per day, Less days (Indirect Proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Persons }}\,30:39 \\ {\text{Working hour/day }}\,{\text{6}}:{\text{5}} \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::12:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 30 \times 6 \times x = 39 \times 5 \times 12 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{ {39 \times 5 \times 12} }}{{ {30 \times 6} }} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 13 \end{aligned}$$

q: A man completes $$\frac{5}{8}$$ of a job in 10 days. At this rate, how many more days will it takes him to finish the job?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Work}}\,{\text{done}} = \frac{5}{8} \\ & {\text{Balance}}\,{\text{work}} = {1 - \frac{5}{8}} = \frac{3}{8} \\ & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{required}}\,{\text{number}}\,{\text{of}}\,{\text{days}}\,{\text{be}}\,x \\ & {\text{Then}}, \\ &\frac{5}{8}:\frac{3}{8} :: 10:x \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{5}{8} \times x = \frac{3}{8} \times 10 \\ & \Rightarrow x = {\frac{3}{8} \times 10 \times \frac{8}{5}} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 6 \end{aligned}$$

q: If a quarter kg of potato costs 60 paise, how many paise will 200 gm cost?
s: $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{Let}}\,{\text{the}}\,{\text{required}}\,{\text{weight}}\,{\text{be}}\,x\,{\text{kg}}. \\ & {\text{Less}}\,{\text{weight,}}\,{\text{less}}\,{\text{cost}}\,\left( {{\text{Direct}}\,{\text{Proportion}}} \right) \\ & \therefore 250:200::60:x \\ & \Rightarrow 250 \times x = {200 \times 60} \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{ {200 \times 60} }}{{250}} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 48 \end{aligned}$$

q: In a dairy farm, 40 cows eat 40 bags of husk in 40 days. In how many days one cow will eat one bag of husk?
s: Let the required number of days be x. Less cows, More days (Indirect Proportion) Less bags, Less days (Direct Proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Cows}}\,\,\,\,\,1:40 \\ {\text{Bags}}\,\,\,\,\,40:1 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::40:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 1 \times 40 \times x = 40 \times 1 \times 40 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 40 \end{aligned}$$

q: A wheel that has 6 cogs is meshed with a larger wheel of 14 cogs. When the smaller wheel has made 21 revolutions, then the number of revolutions mad by the larger wheel is:
s: Let the required number of revolutions made by larger wheel be x . Then, More cogs, Less revolutions (Indirect Proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 14:6::21:x \\ & \Rightarrow 14 \times x = 6 \times 21 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{6 \times 21}}{{14}} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 9 \end{aligned}$$

q: If 7 spiders make 7 webs in 7 days, then 1 spider will make 1 web in how many days?
s: Let the required number days be x. Less spiders, More days (Indirect Proportion) Less webs, Less days (Direct Proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Spiders}}\,\,\,\,\,1:7 \\ \,\,\,{\text{Webs}}\,\,\,\,\,7:1 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::7:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 1 \times 7 \times x = 7 \times 1 \times 7 \\ & \Rightarrow x = 7 \end{aligned}$$

q: A flagstaff 17.5 m high casts a shadow of length 40.25 m. The height of the building, which casts a shadow of length 28.75 m under similar conditions will be:
s: Let the height of the building x metres. Less lengthy shadow, Less in the height (Direct Proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 40.25:28.75::17.5:x \\ & \Rightarrow 40.25 \times x = 28.75 \times 17.5 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{28.75 \times 17.5}}{{40.25}} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 12.5 \end{aligned}$$

q: In a camp, there is a meal for 120 men or 200 children. If 150 children have taken the meal, how many men will be catered to with remaining meal?
s: There is a meal for 200 children 150 children have taken the meal Remaining meal is to be catered to 50 children Now, 200 children = 120 men ∴ 50 children $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{120}}{{200}} \times 50} \right){\text{men}} \\ & = {\text{30 men}} \end{aligned}$$

q: An industrial loom weaves 0.128 metres of cloth every second. Approximately, how many seconds will it take for the loom to weave 25 metres of cloth?
s: Le the required time be x seconds. More metres, More time (Direct Proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 0.128:25::1:x \\ & \Rightarrow 0.128x = 25 \times 1 \\ & x = \frac{{25}}{{0.128}} = \frac{{25 \times 1000}}{{128}} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 195.31 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Required time = 195 sec (approximately)

q: 36 men can complete a piece of work in 18 days. In how many days will 27 men complete the same work?
s: Let the required number of days be x . Less men, More days (Indirect Proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 27:36::18:x \\ & \Rightarrow 27 \times x = 36 \times 18 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{36 \times 18}}{{27}} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 24 \end{aligned}$$

q: 4 mat-weavers can weave 4 mats in 4 days. At the same rate, how many mats would be woven by 8 mat-weavers in 8 days?
s: Let the required number of bottles be x. More weavers, More mats (Direct Proportion) More days, More mats (Direct Proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Wavers}}\,\,\,\,4:8 \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Days}}\,\,\,\,4:8 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::4:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 4 \times 4 \times x = 8 \times 8 \times 4 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{{ {8 \times 8 \times 4} }}{{4 \times 4}} \\ & \Rightarrow x = 16 \end{aligned}$$

q: The price of 357 mangoes is Rs. 1517.25. What will be the approximate price of 49 dozens of such mangoes ?
s: Let the required price be Rs. x More mangoes, More price (Direct proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 357:\left( {49 \times 12} \right)::1517.25:x \\ & \Leftrightarrow 357x = \left( {49 \times 12 \times 1517.25} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {49 \times 12 \times 1517.25} \right)}}{{357}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 2499 \end{aligned}$$ Hence, the approximate price is Rs. 2500

q: An industrial loom weaves 0.128 metres of cloth every second. Approximately, how many seconds will it take for the loom to weave 25 metres of cloth ?
s: Let the required time be x seconds Then, More metres, More time (direct proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 0.128:25::1:x \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{25}}{{0.128}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{25 \times 1000}}{{128}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 195.31 \end{aligned}$$` ∴ Required time =195 seconds (approx)

q: A snapshot $${\text{1}}\frac{7}{8} \times 2\frac{1}{2}$$ is to be enlarged so that the longer dimension is 4. What will be the dimension of the shorter side ?
s: Let the dimension of the shorter side be x More is the longer side, More is the shorter side (Direct proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 2\frac{1}{2}:4::1\frac{7}{8}:x \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{5}{2}x = 4 \times \frac{{15}}{8} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{15}}{2} \times \frac{2}{5}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 3 \end{aligned}$$

q: A canteen requires 651 bananas for a week. Totally, how many bananas will it require for the months of April, May and June ?
s: Total number of days = (30 + 31 + 30) = 91 Let the number of bananas be x More days, More bananas (Direct proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 7:91::651:x \\ & \Rightarrow 7x = 91 \times 651 \\ & \Rightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{91 \times 651}}{7}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow x = 8463 \end{aligned}$$

q: If $$\frac{4}{9}$$ th of a bucket is filled in 1 minute, the rest of it will be filled in ?
s: Remaining part $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {1 - \frac{4}{9}} \right) \\ & = \frac{5}{9}{\text{ }} \end{aligned}$$ Let the required time be x minutes More volume to be filled , More time taken (Direct proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}\frac{4}{9}:\frac{5}{9}::1:x \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{4}{9}x = \frac{5}{9} \\ & \Rightarrow x = \left( {\frac{5}{9} \times \frac{9}{4}} \right) \\ & \Rightarrow x = \frac{5}{4}{\text{ }} \end{aligned}$$

q: On a certain map of India the actual distance of 1450 km between two cities Delhi and Kolkata is shown as 5 cm. What scale is used to draw the map ?
s: 5 cm on the map represents 1450 km ∴ 1 cm on the map represents $$\left( {\frac{{1450}}{5}} \right)$$ km = 290 km Hence, the scale is 1 cm : 290 km i.e., $$1:29 \times {10^6}{\text{ }}$$ $$\left[ {\because 290{\text{km}} = \left( {29 \times {{10}^6}} \right){\text{cm}}} \right]$$

q: A flagstaff 17.5 m high caste a shadow of length 40.25 m. The height of the building, which casts a shadow of length 28.75 m under similar conditions will be ?
s: Let the height of the building be x metres Lees lengthy shadow, Less is the height (Direct proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 40.25:28.75::17.5:x \\ & \Leftrightarrow 40.25 \times x = 28.75 \times 17.5 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {28.75 \times 17.5} \right)}}{{40.25}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 12.5 \end{aligned}$$

q: A man completes $$\frac{5}{8}$$ of a job in 10 days. At this rate, how many more days will it take him to finish the job ?
s: Work done = $$\frac{5}{8}$$ Balance work $$= \left( {1 - \frac{5}{8}} \right)$$ $$= \frac{3}{8}$$ Less work, Less days ( Direct proportion) Let the required number of days be x Then, $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \frac{5}{8}:\frac{3}{8}::10:x \\ & \Leftrightarrow \frac{5}{8} \times x = \frac{3}{8} \times 10 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \left( {\frac{3}{8} \times 10 \times \frac{8}{5}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 6 \end{aligned}$$

q: 56 men can complete a piece of work in 24 days. In how many days can 42 men complete the same piece of work ?
s: Let the required number of days be x Less men, More days (Indirect proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 42:56::24:x \\ & \Leftrightarrow 42 \times x = 56 \times 24 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{56 \times 24}}{{42}}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 32 \end{aligned}$$

q: 30 men can do a piece of work in 16 days. How many men would be required to do the same work in 20 days ?
s: Let the required number of men be x More days, Less men (Indirect proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}20:16::30:x \\ & \Leftrightarrow 20x = 16 \times 30 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{16 \times 30}}{{20}}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 24 \end{aligned}$$

q: 4 mat-weavers can weave 4 mats in 4 days. At the same rate, how many mats would be woven by 8 mat-weavers in 8 days ?
s: Let the required number of mats be x More weavers , More mates ( Direct proportion ) More days, More mats ( Direct proportion ) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Weavers }}4:8 \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Days }}4:8 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::4:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 4 \times 4 \times x = 8 \times 8 \times 4 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {8 \times 8 \times 4} \right)}}{{\left( {4 \times 4} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 16 \end{aligned}$$

q: If 7 maids with 7 mops cleaned 7 floors in 7 hours, how long would it take 3 maids to mop 3 floors with 3 mops ?
s: Since each maid would work with one mop, So,we shall consider 1 maid and 1 mop as 1 unit Let the required time be x hours Less maids and mops, More time (Indirect proportion) Less floor, Less time (Direct proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Maids \& Mops 3}}:7 \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Floors 7}}:3 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::7:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}3 \times 7 \times x = 7 \times 3 \times 7 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {7 \times 3 \times 7} \right)}}{{\left( {3 \times 7} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 7 \end{aligned}$$

q: Four gardeners with four grass mowers mow 400 sq. m of ground in 4 hours. How long would it take for eight gardeners with eight grass mowers to mow 800 sq. m of ground ?
s: Since each gardener would work with one grass mower, So, we shall consider 1 gardener and 1 grass mower as one unit. Let the required time be x hours More gardeners and grass mowers, Less time (Indirect proportion) More area, More time (Direct proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Gardeners \& grass mowers 8}}:4 \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Area 400}}:800 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::4:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}8 \times 400 \times x = 4 \times 800 \times 4 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {4 \times 800 \times 4} \right)}}{{\left( {8 \times 400} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 4 \end{aligned}$$

q: Running at the same constant rate, 6 identical machines can produce a total of 180 bottles per hour. How many bottles could 15 such machines produce on 30 minutes ?
s: Let the required number of bottles be x More machines, More bottles produced (Direct proportion) Less time, Less bottles produce (Direct proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Machines 6}}:15 \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Times 60}}:30 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::180:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}6 \times 60 \times x = 15 \times 30 \times 180 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {15 \times 30 \times 180} \right)}}{{\left( {6 \times 60} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 225 \end{aligned}$$

q: If 6 persons working 8 hours a day earn Rs. 8400 per week, then 9 persons working 6 hours a day will earn per week ?
s: Let the weekly earning be Rs. x More persons , More earning (Direct proportion) Less working hours, Less earning (Direct proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Persons 6}}:9 \\ {\text{Working hours 8}}:6 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::8400:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}6 \times 8 \times x = 9 \times 6 \times 8400 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {9 \times 6 \times 8400} \right)}}{{\left( {6 \times 8} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 9450 \end{aligned}$$

q: If 5 workers can collect 60 kg wheat in 3 days, how many kilograms of wheat will 8 workers collect in 5 days ?
s: Let the required quantity be x kg. More workers, More quantity (Direct proportion) More days, More quantity (Direct proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Workers 5}}:8 \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Days 3}}:5 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::60:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}5 \times 3 \times x = 8 \times 5 \times 60 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {8 \times 5 \times 60} \right)}}{{\left( {5 \times 3} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 160 \end{aligned}$$

q: 50 people consume 350 kg of rice in 30 days. In how many days will 35 people consume 50 kg of rice ?
s: Let the required number of days be x Less people, More days (Indirect proportion) Less quantity, Less days ( Direct proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{People 35}}:50 \\ {\text{Quantity 350}}:50 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::30:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}35 \times 350 \times x = 50 \times 50 \times 30 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {50 \times 50 \times 30} \right)}}{{\left( {35 \times 350} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{300}}{{49}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 6\frac{6}{{49}} \end{aligned}$$

q: Working 8 hours a day, 12 men can do a work in 30 days. Working 4 hours a day, 18 men can do work in ?
s: Let the required number of days be x Less working hours, More days (Indirect Proportion) More men, Less days (Indirect Proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Working hours 4}}:8 \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Men 18}}:12 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::30:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}4 \times 18 \times x = 8 \times 12 \times 30 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {8 \times 12 \times 30} \right)}}{{\left( {4 \times 18} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 40 \end{aligned}$$

q: 5 persons can prepare an admission list in 8 days working 7 hours a day. If 2 persons join them so as to complete the work in 4 days, they need to work per day for ?
s: Let the number of working hours per day be x More persons, Less working hours ( Indirect proportion) Less days, More working hours (Indirect proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Persons 7}}:5 \\ {\text{Quantity 4}}:8 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::7:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}7 \times 4 \times x = 5 \times 8 \times 7 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {5 \times 8 \times 7} \right)}}{{\left( {7 \times 4} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 10 \end{aligned}$$

q: 4 persons can prepare an admission list in 8 days working 7 hours a day. If 3 persons join them so as to complete the work in 4 days, they need to work per day for ?
s: Let the number of working hours per day be x More persons, Less working hours ( Indirect proportion) Less days, More working hours (Indirect proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Persons 7}}:4 \\ {\text{Quantity 4}}:8 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::7:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}7 \times 4 \times x = 4 \times 8 \times 7 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {4 \times 8 \times 7} \right)}}{{\left( {7 \times 4} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 8 \end{aligned}$$

q: 3 pumps , working 8 hours a day, can empty a tank in 2 days. How many hours a day must 4 pumps work to empty the tank in 1 day ?
s: Let the required number of working hours per day be x More pumps, Less working hours per day (Indirect proportion) Less days, More working hours per day (Indirect proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Pumps 4}}:3 \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Days 1}}:2 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::8:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}4 \times 1 \times x = 3 \times 2 \times 8 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {3 \times 2 \times 8} \right)}}{{\left( 4 \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 12 \end{aligned}$$

q: If 5 men or 7 women can earn Rs. 5250 per day, how much would 7 men and 13 women earn per day ?
s: Let the required earning be Rs. x 5 men = 7 women 7 men = $$\left( \frac{7}{5} \times 7 \right)$$ women = $$\frac{49}{5}$$ women ∴ (7 men and 13 women) $$\begin{aligned} & = \left( {\frac{{49}}{5} + 13} \right){\text{women}} \\ & = \frac{{114}}{5}{\text{ women}} \end{aligned}$$ Now, More women, More earning (Direct proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}7 : \frac{{114}}{5}::{\text{ 5}}250 : x \\ & \Leftrightarrow 7x = \left( {\frac{{114}}{5} \times 5250} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow 7x = 119700 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 17100 \end{aligned}$$

q: 3 men or 6 women can do a piece of work in 20 days. In how days will 12 men and 8 women do the same work ?
s: Let the required number of days be x 3 men = 6 women ⇒12 men = (2 × 12) women = 24 women ∴ 12 men and 8 women = (24 + 8) women = 32 women Now, More women, Less days (Indirect Proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}32:6::20:x \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{6 \times 20}}{{32}}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{15}}{4} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 3\frac{3}{4} \end{aligned}$$

q: 49 pumps can empty a reservoir in $$6\frac{1}{2}$$ days, working 8 hours a day. If 196 pumps are used for 5 hours each day, then the same work will be complete in ?
s: Let the required number of days be x Then, More pumps, Less days (Indirect proportion) Less working hour/day, More days (Indirect proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Pumps 196}}:49 \\ {\text{Working hour/day 5}}:8 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::\frac{{13}}{2}:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}196 \times 5 \times x = 49 \times 8 \times \frac{{13}}{2} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \left( {49 \times 8 \times \frac{{13}}{2} \times \frac{1}{{196 \times 5}}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{13}}{5} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 2\frac{3}{5} \end{aligned}$$

q: 30 labourers working 7 hours a day can finish a piece of work in 18 days. If the labourers work 6 hours a day, then the number of labourers to finish the same piece of work in 30 days, will be ?
s: Let the required number of labourers be x Less working hour/day, More labours (Indirect proportion) More days, Less labourers (Indirect proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Working hours/day 6}}:7 \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Days 30}}:18 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::30:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore 6 \times 30 \times x = 7 \times 18 \times 30 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 6x = 126 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 21 \end{aligned}$$

q: If 12 carpenters, working 6 hours a day, can make 460 chairs in 24 days, how many chairs will 18 carpenters make in 36 days, each working 8 hours a day ?
s: Let the required number of chairs be x Then, More carpenters, More chairs (Direct proportion) More hours per day, More chairs (Direct proportion) More days, More chairs (Direct proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} \,\,\,\,{\text{Carpenters 12}}:18 \\ {\text{Hours per day 6}}:8 \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Days 24}}:{\text{36}} \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::460:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}12 \times 6 \times 24 \times x = 18 \times 8 \times 36 \times 460 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {18 \times 8 \times 36 \times 460} \right)}}{{\left( {12 \times 6 \times 24} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 1380 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Required number of chairs = 1380

q: If 5 spiders can catch five files in five minutes, how many files can hundred spiders catch in 100 minutes ?
s: Let the required number of chairs be x. Then, More spiders, More flies (Direct proportion) More time, More flies (Direct proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} \,\,\,{\text{Spiders 5}}:100 \\ {\text{Minutes 5}}:100 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::5:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}5 \times 5 \times x = 100 \times 100 \times 5 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {100 \times 100 \times 5} \right)}}{{\left( {5 \times 5} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 2000 \end{aligned}$$

q: 2 persons working 2 hours a day assemble 2 machine in 2 days. The number of machines assemble by 6 persons working 6 hours a day in 6 day is ?
s: Let the required number of machine be x More persons, More machines (Direct proportion) More working working hours, More machines (Direct proportion) More days, More machines (Direct proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Persons 2}}:6 \\ \,\,\,\, {\text{Working hours 2}}:6 \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Days 2}}:{\text{6}} \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::2:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}2 \times 2 \times 2 \times x = 6 \times 6 \times 6 \times 2 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {6 \times 6 \times 6 \times 2} \right)}}{{\left( {2 \times 2 \times 2} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 54 \end{aligned}$$

q: A wall of 100 meters can be built by 7 men or 10 women in 10 days. How many days will 14 men and 20 women take to build a wall of 600 metres ?
s: Let the required number of days be x 7 men = 10 women (14 men and 20 women) = (20 + 20) women = 40 women More length, More days (Direct proportion) More women, Less days (Indirect proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Length 100}}:600 \\ \,\,{\text{Women 40}}:10 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::10:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}100 \times 40 \times x = 600 \times 10 \times 10 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {600 \times 10 \times 10} \right)}}{{\left( {100 \times 40} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 15 \end{aligned}$$

q: 21 binders can bind 1400 books in 15 days. How many binders will required to bind 800 books in 20 days ?
s: Let the required number of binders be x Less books, Less binders (Direct proportion) More days, Less binders (Indirect proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Books 1400}}:800 \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Days 20}}:15 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::21:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}1400 \times 20 \times x = 800 \times 15 \times 21 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {800 \times 15 \times 21} \right)}}{{\left( {1400 \times 20} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 9 \end{aligned}$$

q: If 17 labourers can dig a ditch 26 m long in 18 days, working 8 hours a day; how many more labourers should be engaged to dig a similar ditch 39 m long in 6 days, each labourer working 9 hours a day ?
s: Let the total number of men to be engaged be $$x$$ More length, More labourers (Direct proportion) Less days, More labourers (Indirect proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Lentgh 26}}:39 \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Days 6}}:18 \\ {\text{Hours per day }}9:8 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::17:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}26 \times 6 \times 9 \times x = 39 \times 18 \times 8 \times 17 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {39 \times 18 \times 8 \times 17} \right)}}{{\left( {26 \times 6 \times 9} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 68 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Number of more labourers = (68 -17) = 51

q: 20 men complete one-third of a piece of work in 20 days. How many more men should be employed to finish the rest of the work in 25 more days ?
s: Let the total number of men be x Work done = $$\frac{1}{3}$$ Remaining work = $$\left( {1 - \frac{1}{3}} \right) = \frac{2}{3}$$ More work, More men (Direct proportion) More days, Less men (Indirect proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} \,{\text{Work }}\frac{1}{3}:\frac{2}{3} \\ {\text{Days 25}}:20 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::20:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}\left( {\frac{1}{3} \times 25 \times x} \right) = \left( {\frac{2}{3} \times 20 \times 20} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{800}}{{25}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 32 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ More men to be employed = (32 - 20) = 12

q: A rope makes 70 rounds of the circumference of a cylinder whose radius of the base is 14 cm. How many times can it go round a cylinder with radius 20 cm ?
s: Let the required number of rounds be x More radius, Less rounds (Indirect proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}20:14::70:x \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {20 \times x} \right) = \left( {14 \times 70} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {14 \times 70} \right)}}{{20}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 49 \end{aligned}$$

q: A contract is to be complete in 46 days and 117 men were set to work, each working 8 hours a day. After 33 days, $$\frac{4}{7}{\text{ }}$$ of the work is completed. How many additional men may be employed so that the work may be completed in time, each man now working 9 hours a day ?
s: Remaining work = $$\left( {1 - \frac{4}{7}} \right){\text{ = }}\frac{3}{7}$$ Remaining period = (46 - 33) = 13 days Let the total men working at it be x Less work, Less men (Direct proportion) Less days, More men (Indirect proportion) More hour/day, Less men (Indirect proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} \,\,\,\,\,{\text{Work }}\frac{4}{7}:\frac{3}{7} \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Men 13}}:33 \\ {\text{Hour/day }}9:8 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::117:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore {\text{ }}\frac{4}{7} \times 13 \times 9 \times x = \frac{3}{7} \times 33 \times 8 \times 117 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {3 \times 33 \times 8 \times 117} \right)}}{{\left( {4 \times 13 \times 9} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 198 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Addition men to be employed = (198 - 117) = 81

q: 12 persons can do a piece of work in 4 days. How many persons are required to complete 8 times the work in half the time ?
s: Let the required number of persons be x Less days , More persons (Indirect proportion) More work , More persons (Direct proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} \,{\text{Days 2}}:4 \\ {\text{Work 1}}:8 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::12:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \,2 \times 1 \times x = 4 \times 8 \times 12 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {4 \times 8 \times 12} \right)}}{{\left( 2 \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 192 \end{aligned}$$

q: If 5 engines consume 6 metric tonnes of coal when each is running 9 hours a day, how many metric tonnes of coal will be needed for 8 engines, each running 10 hours a day, it begin given that 3 engines of the former type consume as much as 4 engines of the latter type ?
s: Let the required quantity of coal be x metric tonnes More engines, More coal (Direct proportion) More hours per day, More coal (Direct proportion) More rate, More coal (Direct proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Engines 5}}:8 \\ {\text{Hours per day 9}}:10 \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Rate }}\frac{1}{3}:\frac{1}{4} \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::6:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \,\,\left( {5 \times 9 \times \frac{1}{3} \times x} \right) = \left( {8 \times 10 \times \frac{1}{4} \times 6} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow 15x = 120 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 8 \end{aligned}$$

q: If 9 men working $${\text{7}}\frac{1}{2}$$ hours a day can finish a piece of work in 20 days, then how many days will be taken by 12 men, working 6 hours a day to finish the work ? (It is being given that 2 men of latter type work as much as 3 men of the former type.)
s: Let the required number of days be x 2 men of latter type = 3 men of former type 12 men of latter type = $$\left( {\frac{3}{2} \times 12} \right)$$ = 18 men of former type More men, Less days (Indirect proportion) Less working hours, More days (Indirect proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Men 18}}:9 \\ {\text{Working hrs 6}}:\frac{{15}}{2} \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::20:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \,18 \times 6 \times x = 9 \times \frac{{15}}{2} \times 20 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 108x = 1350 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{25}}{2} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 12\frac{1}{2} \end{aligned}$$

q: 15 men take 21 days of 8 hours each to do a piece of work. How many days of 6 hours each would 21 women take, 3 women do as much work as 2 men ?
s: 3 women ≡ 2 men So, 21 women ≡ 14 men Less men, More days (Indirect proportion) Less hours per day, More days (Indirect proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Men 14}}:15 \\ {\text{Hours per day 6}}:8 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::21:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \,\left( {14 \times 6 \times x} \right) = \left( {15 \times 8 \times 21} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {15 \times 8 \times 21} \right)}}{{\left( {14 \times 6} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 30 \end{aligned}$$ ∴ Required number of days = 30

q: In a barrack of soldiers there was stock of food for 190 days for 4000 soldiers. After 30 days 800 soldiers left the barrack. For how many days shall the left over food last for the remaining soldiers ?
s: Let the remaining food last for x days 4000 soldiers had provision for 160 days 3200 soldiers had provision for x days Less men, More days (Indirect proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \,3200:4000::160:x \\ & \Leftrightarrow 3200x = 4000 \times 160 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {4000 \times 160} \right)}}{{3200}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 200 \end{aligned}$$

q: A garrison of 500 men had provisions for 27 days. After 3 days a reinforcement of 300 men arrived. For how many more days will the remaining food last now ?
s: Let the remaining food last for x days 500 men had provision for = (27 - 3) = 24 days (500 + 300) men had provision for x days More men, Less days (Indirect proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \,800:500::24:x \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {800 \times x} \right) = \left( {500 \times 24} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {500 \times 24} \right)}}{{800}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 15 \end{aligned}$$

q: A garrison had provision for a certain number of days. After 10 days, $$\frac{1}{5}$$ of the men desert and it is found that the provisions will now last just as long as before. How long was that ?
s: Initially, Let there be x men having food for y days After 10 days, x men had food for days (y - 10) Also, $$\left( {x - \frac{x}{5}} \right)$$ men had food for y days $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \,x\left( {y - 10} \right) = \frac{{4x}}{5} \times y \\ & \Leftrightarrow 5xy - 50x = 4xy \\ & \Leftrightarrow xy - 50x = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x\left( {y - 50} \right) = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow y - 50 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow y = 50 \end{aligned}$$

q: A fort has provisions for 50 days. If after 10 days they are strengthened by 500 men and the food lasts for 35 days longer, the number of men originally in the fort were ?
s: Let there be x men originally So, x men had provisions 40 days whereas (x + 500) men consumed it in 35 days More men, Less days (Indirect proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \,\left( {x + 500} \right):x::40:35 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 35 \times \left( {x + 500} \right) = 40x \\ & \Leftrightarrow 5x = 35 \times 500 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \left( {\frac{{35 \times 500}}{5}} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 3500 \end{aligned}$$

q: A team of workers was employed by a contractor who undertook to finish 360 pieces of an article in a certain number of days. Making four more pieces per day than was planned, they could complete the job a day ahead of schedule. How many days did they take to complete the job ?
s: Let the team take x days to finish 360 pieces Then, number of pieces made each day = $$\frac{{360}}{x}$$ More number of pieces per day, Less days (Indirect proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \,\left( {\frac{{360}}{x} + 4} \right):\frac{{360}}{x}::x:\left( {x - 1} \right) \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {\frac{{360}}{x} + 4} \right) \left( {x - 1} \right) = \frac{{360}}{x} \times x \\ & \Leftrightarrow 360 - \frac{{360}}{x} + 4x - 4 = 360 \\ & \Leftrightarrow 4x - \frac{{360}}{x} - 4 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x - \frac{{90}}{x} - 1 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow {x^2} - x - 90 = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow \left( {x - 10} \right)\left( {x + 9} \right) = 0 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 10 \end{aligned}$$

q: The work done by a women in 8 hours is equal to the work done by a man in 6 hours and by a boy in 12 hours. If working 6 hours per day 9 men can complete a work in 6 days, then in how many days can 12 men, 12 women and 12 boys together finish the same work, working 8 hours per day ?
s: Ratio of time taken by a woman, a man and a boy $$\begin{aligned} & = 8:6:12 \\ & = 4:3:6 \end{aligned}$$ So, 4 women ≡ 3 men ≡ 6 boy (12 mens + 12 womens + 12 boys) $$\begin{aligned} & = \left[ {12 + \left( {\frac{3}{4} \times 12} \right) + \left( {\frac{3}{6} \times 12} \right)} \right]{\text{men}} \\ & {\text{ = }}\left( {12 + 9 + 6} \right){\text{men}} \\ & = 27{\text{ men}} \end{aligned}$$ Let the required number of days be x More men, Less days (Indirect proportion) More working hours, Less days (Indirect proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} {\text{Working hours 8}}:6 \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Men 27}}:9 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::6:x\] $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \,27 \times 8 \times x = 9 \times 6 \times 6 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{\left( {9 \times 6 \times 6} \right)}}{{\left( {27 \times 8} \right)}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{3}{2} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 1\frac{1}{2} \end{aligned}$$

q: 12 men and 18 boys, working $$7\frac{1}{2}$$ hours a day, can do a piece of work in 60 days. If a man works equal to 2 boys, then how many boys will be required to help 21 men to do twice the work in 50 days, working 9 hours a day ?
s: 1 man ≡ 2 boys ⇔ (12 men + 18 boys) ≡ (12 × 2 ×18) boys = 42 boys Let required number of boys = x ⇒ (21 men + x boys) ≡ (21 × 2 × x) boys = (42 + x) boys Less days, More boys (Indirect proportion) More hours per day, Less boys (Indirect proportion) More work, More boys (Direct proportion) \[\left. \begin{gathered} \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Days 50}}:60 \\ {\text{Hours per day 9}}:\frac{{15}}{2} \\ \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{\text{Work }}1:2 \\ \end{gathered} \right\}::42:\left( {42 + x} \right)\] $$\therefore \left[ {50 \times 9 \times 1 \times \left( {42 + x} \right)} \right] =$$ $$\left( {60 \times \frac{{15}}{2} \times 2 \times 42} \right)$$ $$\begin{aligned} & \Leftrightarrow \left( {42 + x} \right) = \frac{{37800}}{{450}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow 42 + x = 84 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 42 \end{aligned}$$

q: Large, medium and small ships are used to bring water. 4 large ships carry as much water as 7 small ships, 3 medium ships carry the same amount of water as 2 large ships and 1 small ship. 15 large, 7 medium and 14 small ships, each made 36 journeys and brought a certain quantity of water. In how many journeys would 12 large, 14 medium and 21 small ships bring the same quantity ?
s: Let, L = large ships, M = medium ships, S = small ships Now from the question, 4L ≡ 7S $$\begin{aligned} & {\text{15L}} = \left( {\frac{7}{4} \times 15} \right){\text{S}} = \frac{{105}}{4}{\text{S}} \\ & {\text{Also, 2L}} = \left( {\frac{7}{4} \times 2} \right){\text{S}} = \frac{7}{2}{\text{S}} \\ & {\text{3M}} \equiv 2{\text{L}} + {\text{1S }} \equiv \left( {\frac{7}{2} + 1} \right){\text{S}} = \frac{9}{2}{\text{S}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow {\text{ 7M}} = \left( {\frac{9}{2} \times \frac{1}{3} \times 7} \right)\,\,{\text{S}} = \frac{{21}}{2}{\text{S}} \\ & \therefore \,\left( {{\text{15L}} + {\text{7M}} + {\text{14S}}} \right){\text{ ships}} \\ & \equiv \left( {\frac{{105}}{4} + \frac{{21}}{2} + 14} \right){\text{S}} \\ & = \frac{{203}}{4}{\text{S}} \\ & \left( {{\text{12 large}} + 14{\text{ medium}} + 2{\text{1 small}}} \right){\text{ ships}} \\ & \equiv \left[ {\left( {\frac{7}{4} \times 12} \right) + \left( {\frac{{21}}{2} \times 2} \right) + 21} \right]{\text{S}} \\ & = \left( {21 + 21 + 21} \right){\text{S}} \\ & = 63\,{\text{S}} \end{aligned}$$ Let the required number of journeys be x More ships, Less journeys (Indirect proportion) $$\begin{aligned} & \therefore \,63:\frac{{203}}{4}::36:x \\ & \Leftrightarrow 63x = \frac{{203}}{4} \times 36 = 1827 \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = \frac{{1827}}{{63}} \\ & \Leftrightarrow x = 29 \end{aligned}$$ Alternate: Now from the question, $$\begin{aligned} & 4L = 7S \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{L}{S} = \frac{7}{4} \\ & \Rightarrow L = 7x;S = 4x \\ & 3M = 2L + S \\ & \Rightarrow M = \frac{{2 \times 7x + 4x}}{3} \\ & \Rightarrow M = 6x \end{aligned}$$ Thus, ratio of large, medium and small = 7 : 6 : 4 So, numbers of journeys: $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{(15 \times 7 + 7 \times 6 + 14 \times 4)36}}{{12 \times 7 + 14 \times 6 + 21 \times 4}} \\ & = \frac{{7308}}{{252}} \\ & = 29 \end{aligned}$$

q: If 2 m, 60 cm cloths is required for one shirt, then the cloth required for 7 shirts is ?
s: Cloth is required for 1 shirt = 2 m, 60 cm or 260 cm Cloth is required for 7 shirt = 260 × 7 = 1820 cm or 18 m 20 cm

q: The cost of 4 dozen papers is Rs. 24. The cost of 1 score of papers (in rupees) is ?
s: 1 score of papers = 20 papers Cost of 4 dozen papers = Rs.24 Cost of 20 papers $$\begin{aligned} & = \frac{{24}}{{4 \times 12}} \times 20 \\ & = {\text{Rs}}{\text{.10}} \end{aligned}$$

q: The cost of 8 fans and 14 ovens is Rs. 36520. What is the cost of 12 fans and 21 ovens ?
s: Cost of 8 fan's and 14 oven's is Rs. 36520 Cost of 4 fan's and 7 oven's is Rs. $$\frac{{{\text{36520}}}}{2}$$ = Rs.18260 Cost of 12 fan's and 21 oven's is = 18260 × 3 = Rs. 54780

q: The cost of 5 kgs of apples is Rs. 450. The cost of 12 dozen mangoes is Rs. 4320 and the cost of 4 kgs of oranges is Rs. 240. What is the total cost of 8 kg of apples, 8 dozen of mangoes and 8 kg of oranges ?
o: Other than those given as option
s: Cost of 5 kgs apples Rs. 450 Cost of 1 kg apples Rs. $$\frac{{{\text{450}}}}{5}$$ Cost of 8 kgs apples = $$\frac{{450}}{5} \times 8$$ = Rs.720 Cost of 12 dozens mangoes Rs. 4320 Cost of 1 dozen mangoes Rs. $$\frac{{{\text{4320}}}}{{12}}$$ Cost of 8 dozen mangoes = $$\frac{{4320}}{{12}} \times 8$$ = Rs. 2880 Cost of 4 kgs oranges = Rs. 240 Cost of 1 kg orange = Rs. $$\frac{{{\text{240}}}}{4}$$ Cost of 8 kgs oranges = $$\frac{{240}}{4} \times 8$$ = Rs. 480 Total cost = 720 + 2880 + 480 = Rs. 4080

q: The cost of 21 pencils and 9 clippers is Rs. 819. The cost price of 7 pencils and 3 clippers is = ?
s: Cost of 21 pencils and 9 clippers = Rs. 819 Cost of 7 pencils and 3 clippers = $$\frac{{819}}{3}$$ = Rs. 273
